To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of DC as a cellular vaccine is an attractive strategy in the treatment of advanced cancers and the use of DC in combination with other immunotherapeutic agents is a promising approach to improve clinical results.

the administration of DC loaded with tumor antigens in patients with advanced cancer is a safe procedure, with a low toxicity profile and with a potential clinical benefit in terms of tumor response, survival and quality of life.

(1) DC-based vaccines are a safe and effective treatment option for patients with advanced solid tumors; (2) DC-based vaccines have a significant clinical impact in patients with advanced melanoma, prostate cancer and renal cancer; (3) the use of DC-based vaccines in patients with advanced breast cancer is still under evaluation; (4) the use of vaccines in patients with hematologic malignancies is still under evaluation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new strategies of DC based therapeutic vaccines, with the goal of improving the efficacy of the treatment and reducing the toxicity of the therapy.
the study of the mechanisms involved in the induction of antitumor immune responses by dendritic cells, as well as the study of the immune responses in cancer patients treated with these vaccines.
the development of new therapeutic strategies in the field of immunotherapy, with the ultimate goal of improving the clinical results in patients with cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of DC-based vaccines has shown promising results, but the data are still limited and need more studies in order to confirm their efficacy.
DC vaccines have shown to be a feasible and safe therapeutic strategy, but their effectiveness is not yet fully established.
the results of the clinical trials of DC-based vaccines are encouraging but not conclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the DC-based vaccines are a promising approach to cancer immunotherapy.
the use of DC-based cancer vaccines is safe and feasible, although the efficacy is still modest.
the DC based immunotherapy is a promising strategy for cancer treatment, but it is not a universal treatment for all types of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the clinical benefit is not directly proportional to the number of DC infused, nor to the route of administration, nor to the type of antigen used.

the clinical response of DC vaccines depends on a variety of factors including the type and source of the DC used for vaccine production, the antigen used, the route of administration, and the schedule of administration.

, although the clinical results of the DC vaccines are not yet comparable to those of other immunotherapies, the DC vaccines have a favorable risk profile and can be used in combination with other immunotherapiesto improve the response rate.
